ownerDecision.request: Yes—12 new concept tanks: three T-80U, T-72B3M and T-72B3 derivatives per country for Ukraine, Poland, China and Russia, with Russia receiving the strongest package.
ownerDecision.scope: Retain unmistakable T-72/T-80 ancestry: original primary donor hull cores, running gear and curved/folded fenders, compact rounded cast turret cores, country-specific bolted armor and bustle additions. Preserve functioning remote machine guns, distinct ERA patterns, lights, sights and equipment. Owner supplied T-72/Moderna visual examples on 2026-10-01, then approved these bases and requested complete structural cheek/flank/rear assemblies plus thick modern skirts wrapping around both track shoulders. Preserve the approved primary cast cores. Revision 5 closes lateral fender/skirt gaps with continuous fitted covers, fits a full-width elevating mantlet, and adds seated national roof/bustle equipment.
ownerDecision.roofRevision: Owner requested 14 national variants including Hetman II and Zubr II, with different roof weapons, paired mantlet lamps, optics, eye/monocle housings and roof equipment. Measurements below include the new stations; primary hulls, fenders and turrets are retained.

ua_t80u_modern.silhouette: Ukrainian T-80U assault modernization: the native low turbine hull and curved fenders carry a compact rounded turret, connected split-chevron cheek and flank housings, a short joined rear return, mounted ERA, assault utility cases, guarded lamps and thick chamfered skirt assemblies joined to the native fenders by fitted shoulder panels. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

ua_t72b3m_modern.silhouette: Ukrainian T-72B3M modernization carrying the complete T-72B3M (2016) turret: its Relikt cheek fan, roof cassettes and bustle boxes, seven Nizh-style module housings clamped on the flank boxes, a slat screen round the rear boxes, two anti-drone roof cage wings, square lamps on raised posts, the monocle sensor, a radome, a command panorama, rear cases, short field whips, the 30 mm shielded command cannon on the commander's cupola and a leafy field net. The native T-72B3M hull keeps its seven thick Ukrainian skirt modules, open hull screens and glacis cassettes.

ua_t72b3_modern.silhouette: Ukrainian T-72B3 field modernization carrying the complete T-72B3 turret: its Kontakt-5 cheeks and roof cassettes, Kontakt-style brick panels on both side stowage cases and a left flank housing, a slat screen round the rear, anti-drone roof cage wings, slit lamps, the flat sensor head and spine sensor, shovel, pry bar, can and tarpaulin roll, short field whips, the 30 mm open fork cannon on the commander's cupola ring and a leafy field net. The original low T-72B3 hull keeps its six removable skirt segments, long side rails and glacis cassettes.

pl_t80u_modern.silhouette: Polish T-80U modernization concept retaining its native low hull and rounded turret ancestry, with a connected ERAWA cheek-and-pannier armor frame, a broad rear basket carrying field stores and a strapped canvas roll, guarded sensors, pannier tool racks, turbine service fittings and thick wraparound skirts joined to the native fenders by continuous fitted shoulders. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

pl_t72b3m_modern.silhouette: Polish T-72B3M heavy modernization concept retaining the native glacis and compact cast turret, with a deep connected cheek-and-bustle armor assembly, three-course ERAWA protection, armored communications cabinets and spare-track stores, guarded sensors and heavy layered skirts with continuous fitted shoulders and front and rear returns. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

pl_t72b3_modern.silhouette: Polish T-72B3 field modernization carrying the complete T-72B3M (2016) turret: its Relikt cheek fan, roof cassettes and bustle boxes, a lower course of ERAWA tiles, slat screens outside the bustle boxes, a short slatted rear rack with the camouflage roll, tools and pack, round lamps, laser-warning heads, a flat sensor head and radome, the 30 mm low-shield remote cannon on the commander's cupola and the Polish field net and leaves. The native T-72B3 hull keeps its layered ERAWA skirts and glacis tiles.

cn_t80u_modern.silhouette: Chinese T-80U turbine modernization carrying the Type 96B turret wrapped in the Yun's own armour: one welded horseshoe housing a side from the nose round the 96B wall and the bustle module's flank, with six broad single-piece chevron ERA cassettes and three flat tiles, a bustle module, rear band and slat cage carrying the drone landing, eight roof smoke tubes on two cradles, service cases on a spine frame, an armoured hood round the gunner's sight, slit lamps on the housings' front shelves, a monocle eye, side electronics, the box sight riding the mantlet and the 12.7 mm faceted station on its own left-roof seat. The original turbine hull keeps six thick layered skirt modules, glacis tiles, twin cooling panels, a slatted transom and two small transverse fuel drums.

cn_t72b3m_modern.silhouette: Chinese T-72B3M modernization carrying the complete Type 96B turret with its special chevron ERA laid over both front wedges, two Shtora-style infrared dazzler heads flanking the mantlet with square guarded lamps on their hoods, a QJC-88 12.7 mm machine gun on an open pintle at the commander's cupola behind its light shield, the box sight riding the mantlet, a scanner head, service cases and an open rear maintenance cage with its three-cell console. The low T-72B3M hull keeps seven thick staggered skirt modules, a glacis ERA course and large transverse auxiliary fuel drums.

cn_t72b3_modern.silhouette: Chinese T-72B3 field modernization carrying the production ZTZ-99A2 turret with its bustle shortened by a tenth and wrapped in the Qilin's own add-ons: one welded flank sleeve a side from the rear armour box to a triangular brow on the side cassette, carrying four chevron ERA cassettes, the side rail and three flat tiles, a bustle roof plate with a small rack and roll, a flat eye, a split-panel sensor on the crown's centre, round guarded lamps, a side camera, field-service boxes and a carrier, an open rear basket carrying the drone landing, and a QJC-88 12.7 mm machine gun on an open pintle at the commander's cupola behind its shield. The original low T-72B3 hull keeps five ribbed layered skirt modules, a glacis ERA course and two individually cradled rear fuel drums.

ru_t80u_modern.silhouette: Bars-M: T-80U turbine hull and compact cast turret with a connected heavy cheek/flank/rear armor housing beneath two-course ERA, round protection sensors, broad rear cage and deep chamfered side skirts wrapping around both track ends. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

ru_t72b3m_modern.silhouette: Bulat-M: T-72B3M low hull and cast-core turret with a deep continuous armored cheek-and-command-bustle enclosure, layered ERA, thick wraparound side armor with soft lower packets and protected panoramic sensors. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

ru_t72b3_modern.silhouette: Bastion-M: compact T-72B3 hull and rounded turret with a compact connected cheek-and-pannier armor frame, broad cheek banks, fine side cassettes, thick returned skirt modules, a short open basket and rectangular sight guards. Distinct mounted roof weapon, paired guarded mantlet lamps, dedicated observation optics and roof sensor installation.

previousDesign.status: Owner retained the native bases and full surrounding armor; requested closure of fender/skirt gaps, closer mantlet fit, and substantially more roof/bustle equipment. Revision 4 superseded before publication.

designInfluences.use: Oplot/Bulat modernization vocabulary; compact cast-core assault, command and field-kit concepts.
PT-91M2 modernization and ERAWA-style modular tile language; cast-core turrets with bolted ERAWA armor and native hulls.
Type-99A swept armor vocabulary; limited wedge armor over visible rounded core and original low hulls.
T-90M modernization vocabulary; heavy layered cheek banks, protected sensors and compact rear packages over cast cores.

ownerAmendments.request: Lower all fourteen national variant turrets to reduce the exposed cylinder between hull and turret. Preserve the other new designs and roof equipment.
